summary: A 100-ft CCC-built Aermotor steel tower from 1935 on Nebraska's Valentine NWR, used for a 1937 fire watch and now reached by a walking trail to an observation deck.

staffing.status: fire watch established 1937; end of staffing not documented

access.note: Walking trail leads to an observation deck on the old fire tower; refuge rates the trail easy

visit.trail_note: Civilian Conservation Corps Fire Tower Trail, 0.66 mi, easy; starts at the parking area at the west end of Hackberry Lake

events.note: Erected by the CCC as a Type MC-39 Aermotor steel tower, 100 ft high
August 1937 CCC report: fire watch established in the Hackberry tower; phone installed but not yet connected
Observation deck added to the tower to accommodate visitors

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The refuge trails page calls the walk the Civilian Conservation Corps Nature Trail in its description and the Civilian Conservation Corps Fire Tower Trail in its trail listing. Both start at the parking area at the west end of Hackberry Lake, so they appear to be one route. The story uses the listing name.

sources.title: Valentine National Wildlife Refuge, Visit Us: Trails

notes_for_editor: Build year (1935), CCC origin and registration rest on the NHLR entry; the same text appears on westlookouts.weebly.com, which is not cited separately. The only lookout-era record found is one August 1937 CCC work report, so staffing, end of fire watch, and any notable fire remain unknown. Nothing found says whether the cab survives in its original form. The brief's access 'unknown' is now public via the trail to the observation deck. height_m is converted from 100 ft. wheninyourstate.com returned HTTP 403 and was not used. No NPS or Nebraska Game and Parks history was checked.
